home.title: Big Cube Solver - every cube from 2×2 to 15×15
home.lead: Point your phone's camera at any cube from 2×2 to 15×15 and follow a short solution, move by move, on a 3D cube - with the real one in your hands.
home.soon: Android · coming soon to Google Play
home.what.sub: Most solvers stop at 6×6 or 7×7. This one keeps going to 15×15 - and it runs on modest phones too, from Android 10 up.
home.f1.d: Custom solvers reduce a 15×15 to a 13×13, then 11×11 ... down to a 3×3, so you never wade through thousands of needless moves.
home.f2.d: Animated 3D moves you can step, rewind, slow down or speed up, in chapters: centres, edges, the final 3×3.
home.f3.d: Turned centres are solved too, so every photo or logo comes back whole and upright.
home.f4.d: Show each face and the colours are read automatically - odd colour schemes are read as they are.
home.f5.d: Spirals, rings, checkerboards, cubes in cubes on every size - and your own, shared as a link.
home.f6.d: Draw on a face or place stickers one by one, and the app finds the moves.
home.f7.d: Connect a Bluetooth smart cube (GAN, Giiker, QiYi, Rubik's Connected): the screen follows every turn, guides each move and times your solves. Put a picture skin on it - the pictures turn with your cube.
home.f8.d: One app for every size, from a pocket 2×2 to a 15×15. No ads, no telemetry - buy once, use forever.
home.turns.sub: Average turns to solve a random cube with the short solver. A regular solver answers in seconds on any phone, with more moves - choose per size.
home.tiers.sub: No subscription, no ads, no account, no telemetry. Software as it used to be: buy it once, use it forever.
home.free.d: Forever. Sticker-sheet picture cubes to turn and scramble included.
home.t15.d: Every size from 2×2 to 15×15, plus picture-cube solving and smart cubes.

faq.title: Q&A - Big Cube Solver
faq.cubes:
Which cubes does it solve?

Every standard cube from 2×2 to 15×15, plus 3×3 picture cubes, where the centres must also face the right way.
faq.phones:
Which phones does it run on?

Android 10 or newer. It was built to run on modest phones too - a 15×15 included.
faq.iphone:
Is there an iPhone version?

Not for now - Big Cube Solver is Android only.
faq.when:
When will it be on Google Play?

Soon. It is in testing now. You can try it before everyone else: become a tester.
faq.price:
How much does it cost?

2×2, 3×3 and 4×4 are free, forever. The bigger sizes are one-time purchases: up to 10×10, or up to 15×15 with picture cubes and smart cubes. No subscription and no ads; the prices will be shown in Google Play.
faq.data:
Does it need the internet? Does it collect data?

No and no. Scanning and solving happen on the phone, the app has no account, ads or tracking, and nothing leaves your phone. Details in the privacy policy.
faq.moves:
How many moves are the solutions?

About 19 turns for a 3×3, 43 for a 4×4, 69 for a 5×5, 200 for a 7×7, 620 for a 10×10 and 1,750 for a 15×15, on average.
faq.why15:
Why does a 15×15 need so many moves?

A 15×15 has 1,014 centre pieces and 156 edge pieces to bring home - a 3×3 has none of the first kind. The app reduces the cube step by step (15×15 to 13×13, to 11×11 ... to 3×3) to keep the count as low as it can.
faq.short:
Short or regular solver - which should I use?

The short solver finds far fewer moves; the regular one answers in seconds on any phone. The first time you open the app the short solvers get ready in the background (about a minute, longer on older phones). You can choose per size.
faq.notation:
Which notation does it use?

Standard (WCA) notation: R, U', F2, wide turns such as 3Rw, and x, y, z for turning the whole cube. Every move is also animated on the 3D cube, so you never need to read it.
faq.tips:
Tips for scanning my cube

Use even light without glare or strong shadows, hold each face straight and let it fill the guide. Cubes with unusual colours are read as they are. If a sticker is read wrong, correct it before solving.
faq.smart:
Which smart cubes work?

Several Bluetooth smart cubes, including Giiker, GAN and QiYi models: the screen follows every turn you make. If yours does not connect, tell us its brand and model at support.
faq.location:
Why does it ask for location with Bluetooth?

On Android 10 and 11, Android itself requires the location permission to look for Bluetooth devices. The app never reads your location.
faq.share:
How do I share a pattern?

In the app, long-press a pattern in My patterns and choose Share: it becomes a link. Whoever opens it on an Android phone with the app gets it in their My patterns. More in Patterns.
faq.more: Not answered here? Write to support.

test.title: Be a tester - Big Cube Solver
test.h1: Test Big Cube Solver before anyone else
test.intro: The app solves any cube from 2×2 to 15×15. Before it goes on Google Play it needs testers. Three steps on your Android phone (Android 10 or newer), with the same Google account you use in the Play Store.
test.s1.d: Open the group and tap Ask to join group. We approve each request by hand, usually the same day; wait for the approval email before step 2. Nobody else sees your email.
test.s2.d: Tap Become a tester. If it says it is not available, wait a few minutes after step 1 and try again.
test.s3.d: From Google Play, like any app. Updates arrive by themselves.
test.ask: One important favour: keep the app installed for at least 14 days and open it now and then. Google requires 12 testers for 14 days in a row before it allows publishing.
test.tell.d: Everything helps: what you liked, what failed, what was unclear. It takes two minutes.
test.q1.d: The phone uses a different Google account than the one that joined the group. In the Play Store tap your picture, switch to that account and repeat step 3.
test.q2.d: For now the app is Android only.
test.q3.h: Is it free? Does it collect data?
test.q3.d: The test version is free. The app has no ads or accounts and sends nothing over the internet: privacy policy.
guide.title: What to try - Big Cube Solver
guide.intro: No need to try everything. What helps most: use the app as you really would, and tell us what happened.
guide.1.d: Pick a size (the size button), tap the dice to scramble and the wand to solve. Try a big one: 10×10 or 15×15. In the test every size is unlocked.
guide.2.d: Tap the camera and show each face. Works best in good light without glare. Tell us your cube size and whether it read the colours right.
guide.3.h: Follow the solution with the cube in your hands
guide.3.d: Step move by move, change the speed, go back. Is every turn clear? Did your cube end up solved?
guide.4.d: Menu → Patterns: form one on your cube. In My patterns save the cube on screen and share it as a link with another tester.
guide.5.h: If you have one: a picture cube or a smart cube
guide.5.d: Picture cube: photograph it solved, then scrambled. Bluetooth smart cube: connect it and follow a guided solution.
guide.6.d: Turn the cube on screen with your finger until it is solved... and see what happens.
guide.wrong.2: If the app closes by itself, it shows a report the next time it opens: share it.
guide.wrong.3: Tell us your phone model, what you did and what you expected.

num.title: Your cube in numbers
num.intro: What grows when a cube gets bigger, from 2×2 to 15×15 - and what this app does with it.
num.pieces_text: Every cube has 8 corners. Edges grow with the size, 12 × (N − 2), and centres with its square, 6 × (N − 2)². A 15×15 has 1,178 pieces you can see: 8 corners, 156 edges and 1,014 centres, with 1,350 stickers.
num.formula_title: How many ways can a 3×3 be mixed?
num.term_twists: each corner twisted 3 ways - 7 freely, the last one follows (2,187)
num.term_flips: each edge flipped 2 ways - 11 freely, the last one follows (2,048)
num.term_parity: pieces can only swap in pairs, so half of those orders cannot happen
num.formula_text: About 43 quintillion. Checking a billion of them every second would take about 1,370 years - yet every one of them can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.
num.formula_general: Bigger cubes use the same idea. Each set of 24 edges or 24 centres that can trade places adds a factor of 24!, divided by 4!⁶ for centres, because the four of each colour look alike. An even cube has no fixed centre, so one corner is held still.
num.positions_text: Each step up the scale is a factor of ten, so the bars grow far faster than they look. A 2×2 has 3.7 million positions, a 3×3 43 quintillion (10¹⁹). From 6×6 up there are more positions than atoms in the observable universe, and a 15×15 has about 7.5 × 10⁸¹³.
num.15_in_full: The 15×15, written out in full ({a} digits):
num.15_universe: Now picture it as a length: {a} millimetres. The observable universe is about 93 billion light-years across, or {b} mm. A line that long would cross the whole universe {c} times - and even that count has {d} digits.
num.turns_text: The app's two solvers (Menu → Solver), the average over many random scrambles. A 3×3 takes about 19 moves. On a 15×15 the short solver finds about 1,750 and the regular one about 2,900.
num.time_text: Seconds on a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7, the middle of nine solves, on a scale of tens: each line is ten times the one below. Up to 4×4 the answer comes in a moment; a 15×15 takes about 11 seconds for the short solution and under 2 for the regular one. The regular solver is so quick that its times jump from size to size with the method each size uses. An older phone can take 20 times longer.
num.deck_title: How big is one deck of cards?
num.deck_intro: Everyone has shuffled a deck of cards. It turns out to be the best way to feel how big a cube is.
num.deck_tap: Tap the cards to shuffle them.
num.deck_count: The first card can be any of 52, the next any of the 51 left, then 50, and so on down to 1. So a deck can be put in order in 52 × 51 × 50 × … × 1 ways, written 52! ("52 factorial"):
num.deck_never: That is about 8 × 10⁶⁷, a number with 68 digits. Every time you shuffle a deck well, the order you get has almost certainly never existed before in the history of the world - and will almost certainly never come up again. The order on screen right now is very likely the first of its kind.
num.deck_scale_sand: Grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches
num.deck_scale_shuffles: Shuffles if everyone alive shuffled every second since the Big Bang
num.deck_scale_deck: Ways to order ONE deck of cards
num.deck_scale_text: Each bar shows how many digits the number has. If all 8 billion people alive had shuffled a deck once a second since the Big Bang, 13.8 billion years ago, they would have seen fewer than one in 10,000 trillion trillion trillion of the possible orders.
num.decks_title: Your cube in decks of cards
num.decks_text: Small cubes fit in a handful of cards: a 2×2 has about as many positions as there are ways to order 10 cards, and a 3×3 matches 21 cards - less than half a deck. From the 5×5 on, one deck is no longer enough: count how many decks, shuffled one after another, give as many possibilities as the cube.
num.decks_15_more: Shuffle 12 decks, one after another, and write down every order. Guessing a scrambled 15×15 without looking is like calling all 12 orders right - all 624 cards, without a single mistake. Each one of those decks is already a first in history.
num.pic_intro: Remember the screen of the Nokia 3310? 84 × 48 pixels, each one either dark or light, on that green backlight.
num.pic_tap: Tap the screen for another picture.
num.pic_headline: A 15×15 has as many positions as the top two-thirds of that screen has pictures.
num.pic_explain: Those 84 × 32 pixels can show about 10⁸⁰⁹ different pictures - every drawing, every word, every face that fits, and endless static. A 15×15 has about 10⁸¹⁴ positions: the same league. It compares how many, not what they look like - but it means you could give every scramble of your 15×15 its own picture on that little screen.
num.pic_rung_3: 3×3 - a chessboard, each square black or white
num.pic_ladder_text: Each picture is drawn at its true size in pixels, and can show about as many different images as its cube has positions. Tap them for new ones. The 3×3 has 2.3 times as many positions as there are ways to colour a chessboard black and white.
num.pic_twist_title: And the screen in your hand?
num.pic_twist: Screens soon left the cube far behind. The very first PC colour screen (CGA, 1981) could show a number of pictures with 47 times as many digits as the 15×15's count. A Full HD screen, 1920 × 1080 pixels in 16.7 million colours, can show 10 to the power 14,981,179 pictures - a number with 15 million digits. That is every photo ever taken or yet to come, and every frame of every film. Matching that would take 18,407 15×15 cubes, all scrambled at once.

num.home: How big is a 15×15, really? Your cube in numbers: pieces, positions, moves and time, from 2×2 to 15×15.

These terms apply to the Big Cube Solver app for Android ("the app") and to this website. The app is developed by the Big Cube Solver team ("we"). By installing or using the app you agree to these terms. Questions: support@bigcubesolver.com.

2. Free and paid features

Solving 2×2, 3×3 and 4×4 cubes is free. Bigger sizes and some features may be offered as one-time purchases inside the app. There are no subscriptions and no ads.

Test versions are shared before release to find problems. They may contain errors, change or stop working, and features may change before or after the public release.

Cubes, patterns, photos and sticker sheets you create or import stay on your phone unless you choose to share them. You are responsible for what you import and share: use only images you have the right to use. Pattern links you share can be opened by anyone who receives them.

5. Other services

Google Play, Discord and the makers of smart cubes are independent of us, and their own terms and policies apply when you use them. Product and brand names (such as GAN, Giiker, QiYi and Rubik's) belong to their owners and are used only to say which cubes work with the app.

6. Solutions and availability

We work hard to give correct, short solutions, but the app is provided "as is": we cannot promise it will be free of errors, work on every device, or always be available. If a solution looks wrong, please tell us at support.

7. Liability

To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from use of the app. Our total liability for any claim is limited to the amount you paid for the app's purchases. This does not exclude liability that cannot be excluded by law.

8. Privacy

The app collects no personal data. Details are in the privacy policy.

9. Changes

We may update these terms, for example when new features or purchases are added. The date at the top shows the current version; important changes will also be announced in the app or on our community server.
